incidents.vector: Attacker abused Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN auth-bypass flaws to make rogue peering connections to SD-WAN Manager devices, then exploited a zero-day (CVE-2026-20245) to escalate to root and create a hidden administrative account.
incidents.impact: Gained root control of the provider's SD-WAN orchestrator, giving stealthy visibility into internal enterprise traffic; extensive anti-forensics (deleted files, reverted configs) prevented investigators from assessing the full scope.

incidents.victim: Fortinet FortiGate firewall/VPN users worldwide (incl. a Turkish NATO defense contractor)
incidents.vector: The 'FortiBleed' campaign ran roughly 1.16 billion credential attempts against 320,000+ FortiGate targets, intercepted SSL VPN authentication hashes, cracked them offline on a 45-GPU cluster, and used recovered admin/VPN credentials to reach internal Active Directory environments.
incidents.impact: Valid admin and VPN credentials for roughly 74,000 FortiGate firewalls across 194 countries were exposed; classified documents were allegedly exfiltrated from a Turkish NATO defense contractor. Australia's ACSC issued a critical alert urging immediate credential rotation.

incidents.vector: Compromise of a third-party firm managing the agency's mobile device management (MDM) platform, tied to exploitation of internet-facing Ivanti EPMM servers.
incidents.impact: Names, phone numbers, and email addresses of Belgian intelligence service employees — plus mobile phone details of officials — were stolen.

incidents.vector: Data-theft and extortion intrusion; the World Leaks group (rebrand of Hunters International) claims it stole more than 200,000 documents and listed the company on its leak site.
incidents.impact: Tata confirmed a security incident; leaked samples allegedly include Apple supplier specifications and Tesla-related manufacturing documents. Tata says operations were unaffected and the data's authenticity is unverified.

incidents.vector: Operation Endgame — a coordinated Microsoft Digital Crimes Unit and Europol action seizing 326 servers and 142 domains powering the SocGholish, Amadey, and StealC malware 'assembly line' used for initial access, credential theft, and ransomware staging.
incidents.impact: Disrupted infrastructure feeding ransomware and fraud campaigns; investigators recovered ~27 million stolen credentials, seized €41M ($47M) in cryptocurrency, and identified 18,000 victim machines.

incidents.victim: Klue customers: Huntress, LastPass, HackerOne, Recorded Future, Jamf, Snyk, OneTrust, Tanium, Gong and others
incidents.vector: The Icarus group breached market-intelligence vendor Klue and abused its OAuth tokens and Salesforce integration to pull customers' Salesforce CRM data.
incidents.impact: Multiple technology and security firms had Salesforce CRM data (contacts, sales records, pricing data) stolen; Icarus is leaking data on its dark web site and extorting victims, raising the risk of targeted social-engineering follow-on.

incidents.victim: Transport for London (TfL); also M&S, Harrods, Co-op, SSM Health, Sutter Health
incidents.vector: Two members of the Scattered Spider crew pleaded guilty to the September 2024 TfL intrusion, which relied on social engineering and credential theft (historically SIM-swapping and SMS/voice phishing).
incidents.impact: The TfL attack disrupted services for months, forced 28,000 employees to reset passwords in person, exposed Oyster refund customer data, and cost ~£29M ($38M). The broader group extorted $115M+ across 47 US entities.

incidents.victim: Millions of consumer Android TV boxes; organizations hit by mass data scraping
incidents.vector: A malicious pre-installed SDK (the Popa plugin of the Vo1d / Badbox 2.0 botnet) on cheap Android TV streaming boxes enrolls devices into a residential proxy pool that relays traffic for ad fraud, account takeovers, and mass scraping.
incidents.impact: Millions of TV boxes forced to relay malicious traffic; a May 2026 scraping event spanned 1.4M+ IPs. Researchers tie revived control domains to a publicly traded Israeli proxy firm, which disputes the characterization.

incidents.victim: OpenClaw AI agent users (developers, macOS users, cryptocurrency holders)
incidents.vector: Malicious 'skills' on the ClawHub AI-agent marketplace used semantic instruction hijacking and curl-pipe-bash lures to trick the AI agent into fetching and running macOS infostealers (AMOS/cluw), with file-padding tricks to evade marketplace scanning.
incidents.impact: Five unblocked malicious skills delivered infostealers to active command-and-control servers before OpenClaw removed them; earlier waves involved 341+ malicious skills, with roughly 17% of analyzed skills carrying payloads.

incidents.victim: Bank Melli, Bank Tejarat, Bank Saderat, Export Development Bank of Iran
incidents.vector: Cyberattack targeting communications infrastructure shared by four of Iran's largest banks.
incidents.impact: Online portals and mobile apps for the four banks were knocked offline over a weekend; the Iranian banking council said no customer data was accessed.

incidents.victim: Chinese-speaking users in China and abroad
incidents.vector: The Silver Fox crew used malspam and fake app-download/phishing sites to lure victims into installing a trojan that deployed infostealers and custom remote-access tools to steal funds.
incidents.impact: Chinese police arrested 67 suspects across five provinces, including the malware author, disrupting one of China's largest active domestic cybercrime operations.

incidents.victim: North American academic, medical, and military research institutions
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited externally facing REDCap research servers, deployed custom malware to harvest credentials, pivoted to domain admin, and abused Google Workspace content-compliance rules to silently BCC-forward sensitive emails for exfiltration.
incidents.impact: A China-nexus actor remained undetected for over a year, targeting national-security, Indo-Pacific command, AI, uncrewed-vehicle, and medical-research data across multiple US and Canadian organizations.

incidents.victim: Oracle PeopleSoft customers: universities, Council of Europe, Ralph Lauren, JCPenney, Nexstar, University of Nottingham
incidents.vector: The ShinyHunters group exploited a critical zero-day in Oracle PeopleSoft (CVE-2026-35273, CVSS 9.8; now in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog) to gain remote code execution, then deployed disguised remote-management agents and credential-spraying scripts to steal data.
incidents.impact: 100+ organizations compromised (heavily higher education); stolen data published on the group's leak site. The University of Nottingham confirmed 40GB+ of data on 450,000+ students and alumni was taken.

incidents.vector: Attackers gained access to parts of the internal network; the company took systems offline to evict them.
incidents.impact: Some sensitive data, including patient personal information, was copied during the intrusion at the maker of Ozempic and Wegovy.

incidents.victim: Arch Linux users installing affected AUR packages
incidents.vector: Attacker abused the Arch User Repository's orphaned-package adoption mechanism to take over abandoned packages and inject a malicious script that downloads a rootkit and infostealer during installation.
incidents.impact: More than 1,900 AUR packages hijacked to deploy a rootkit plus credential harvester that steals browser, Electron app, and developer secrets; hijacking attempts are ongoing.

incidents.victim: 1.2M+ websites using OptinMonster, TrustPulse, and PushEngage plugins
incidents.vector: Malicious code planted in three legitimate Awesome Motive WordPress plugins waits for an admin login, then creates a rogue admin account and installs a self-hiding backdoor plugin.
incidents.impact: More than 1.2 million websites were backdoored, granting attackers persistent administrative access.

incidents.victim: Global Schools Group (65 K-12 campuses across nine countries)
incidents.vector: Data was exfiltrated from an unsecured database exposed online, followed by a failed ransom negotiation and a public leak.
incidents.impact: Terabytes of data leaked, including passport details of children and parents, attendance records, teacher passwords, and photos of campus visitors.

incidents.victim: 1,000+ Conti ransomware victims across 47 US states and 31 countries
incidents.vector: Conti conspirators hacked into victim networks, encrypted data, and demanded ransom; a Ukrainian national who coded a malware loader and handled stolen data was extradited from Ireland.
incidents.impact: Conti caused at least $150M in ransom payments; the conspirator pleaded guilty to wire fraud conspiracy and faces up to 20 years, with sentencing set for September 10, 2026.

incidents.victim: Organizations running Ivanti Sentry (incl. US federal agencies)
incidents.vector: An OS command-injection flaw in Ivanti Sentry (CVE-2026-10520) lets an attacker execute arbitrary commands on the appliance.
incidents.impact: CISA added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog based on evidence of active exploitation and mandated rapid federal remediation under BOD 26-04.
